text:
aj: morning async — short standup

aj: what I did: merged microkernel prefetch fix (reconciles kv index + memmap), ran a couple of end-to-end batch perf runs on staging.
aj: blockers: seeing KV eviction spikes at p99 when batch sizes hit ~256 and seq len >= 128, curious if it's thrashing or a corner in the eviction loop.
aj: today: iterate on eviction heuristics, open canary PR for a softened eviction policy, need a pair to run a repeatable repro on dedicated. cc @sasha

sasha: thanks — can you paste the staging run logs + PR link? also want to know if this is hotspot in allocator or in async batch aggregator.

aj: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4123 (WIP) — main change is `soft_evict=true` toggle + metrics + an opt-in sampling flag.

aj: quick paste from the failing bench run: 
```
./bench --model small-llama --seq 128 --batch 256 --kv-enabled
Throughput: 9.4k tok/s
p50: 95ms  p95: 260ms  p99: 490ms
KV hit-rate: 0.72
GC/evict spikes observed at 00:12:43
```

liam: I can run the same binary on a dedicated pool later today. can you capture `top` and `perf` while it's running? suspecting lock contention on the LRU list.

maria: quick note — I tried bumping `kv_ttl` from 10s->20s in a local cluster, throughput didn't move much but hit-rate improved slightly. doesn't fully explain p99.

aj: yep TTL tweak gave small win. eviction count still jumps under sustained micro-bursts.

liam: suggestion: add a soft-evict phase that marks items for delayed eviction and a background compactor that frees when memory pressure crosses threshold. low-risk toggle for canary.

sasha: agree. also we should add a metric `eviction_latency_ms` to trace the expensive path. add to PR.

aj: added `eviction_latency_ms` to the PR and a simple histogram. pushed a small patch (force-push).

ci-bot: CI: All checks passed for commit 3b9f2e1 — unit tests and integration smoke. :white_check_mark:

liam: i'll spin up a dedicated 4xA10 pool and run 3 repeats (seq 128 batch [64,128,256]) and post results. planning to seed with synthetic hot prefixes to stress the KV.

maria: i'll review the PR and look at the histogram output schema — want to make sure it's compatible with the existing tracing pipeline.

sasha: for rollout plan: canary = 5% traffic -> 25% -> full if no regressions for 2 hours. include automatic rollback if p99 increases > 15% or error rate spikes. I'll add a rollout config in the PR description.

aj: pinging reviewers: @maria @liam — small reviewers notes in PR. would appreciate a quick thumbs so we can canary this afternoon.

maria: i'll review in ~30m.

liam: running first pass now, will share raw bench outputs.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: serving-canary-2026-03-17T15:20Z -> 5% traffic. Monitor window 120m.

aj: thanks everyone. if liam sees the eviction spike on dedicated we'll try the soft-evict toggle and compare. otherwise i'll instrument a finer-grain trace to find the hot lock.

sasha: small logistics — if we need an oncall from eng-sre during the canary, tag @oncall in the PR and i'll loop them in.

aj: done. closing this thread for now — will post bench outputs and a follow-up thread with canary results. :thumbsup:
